why: Court states that on an ex-parte decree the defendant may apply under Order IX Rule 13 to set it aside by showing non-service or sufficient cause.

span: Two remedies were available to the defendant
why: Recital within the facts that the defendant had two remedies, one under Order IX Rule 13; the court's reasoning follows in later paragraphs.

span: the petition ﬁ led under Order IX Rule 13 CPC seeking setting aside of the ex-parte decree was also dismissed
why: Headnote issue for consideration listing the lower courts' orders; the Supreme Court's decision is not in this passage.

span: application filed by appellants-defendants under Or.IX, r.13 CPC allowed
why: Headnote holding that the Supreme Court allowed the defendants' Order IX Rule 13 application and restored the suit; headnote confidence is capped.

span: Pursuing the proceedings in the application filed under Order IX Rule 13 CPC has caused further delay of 270 days.
why: Headnote on delay in filing a first appeal after an Order IX Rule 13 application failed; it does not state whether the remedy is available.

span: an appeal only against the refusal to set aside the ex-parte decree is maintainable whereas if an order allowing such an application is passed, the same is not appealable
why: Court explains appealability of orders under Order IX Rule 13, not whether the application can succeed.

span: The appellants – original defendant nos. 2 & 3 moved an impleadment application in the suit which was allowed.
why: Procedural history of an ex-parte judgment for failure to file a written statement; the Supreme Court's view appears in the next paragraph.

span: the Court may put the defendant to terms as to costs, payment into Court or otherwise
why: Court discusses terms that may be imposed when setting aside an ex-parte decree; it does not itself affirm or refuse the remedy in this passage.

span: The Commercial Courts Act does not amend Order 43 Rule 1 of the CPC
why: Appealability of orders under the Commercial Courts Act and Order 43; Order IX Rule 13 appears only in a quoted list.

span: Time spent in pursuing the application u/Or. IX r.13 to set aside the ex-parte decree to be taken as “sufficient cause”
why: Headnote on the relation between an Order IX Rule 13 application and a regular appeal; it treats the application as a remedy but does not decide whether it succeeds.
